title: Bind trusted workspace overlays to canonical repository identity
description:
## Finding

The trusted `[workspace.<slug>]` configuration layer is selected from only the slugified repository directory basename. Two unrelated repositories with the same basename—or names that differ only by punctuation/case—therefore receive the same trusted overlay.

That overlay controls command execution and security authority: merge/PR gates, target branches, Git behavior, CI autofix, issue autopilot, hooks, sandbox mounts, coding-agent accounts, environment bundles, and MCP scope ceilings. The code has a collision-aware DB repository slug elsewhere, but the trusted config resolver does not use it.

## Evidence at audited commit `299fc13ee53f31bdeb99bbf35609a6ad55528973`

* `crates/thegn-core/src/config.rs:989-1001` defines `workspace_slug(repo_root)` as `slugify(repo_name(repo_root))`, falling back to `repo`; parent path, canonical origin, DB repository identity, and generation are absent.
* `WorkspaceConfig` at `config.rs:2320-2385` carries accounts, hooks, sandbox mounts, env bundle, merge queue, PR queue, CI, autopilot, Git, and MCP authorization settings.
* `Config::repo_merge_queue`, `repo_git`, `repo_pr_queue`, `repo_ci`, and `repo_autopilot` at `config.rs:6467-6541` all select by the basename slug.
* `config_resolve.rs:1171-1187` adds trusted workspace sandbox mounts by that same key after the untrusted repo overlay clamp, so a colliding repo receives higher-trust ungated mounts.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/worktree_lifecycle.rs:250-273` selects trusted workspace hooks by the same key.
* Account and environment-bundle selection consume `[workspace.<slug>]`, so the collision can redirect credential homes/HOME identity.
* CLI explain/write paths in `cmd/config.rs` and `cmd/merge.rs` also derive the key from basename, reinforcing the ambiguity instead of detecting it.
* Tests at `config_tests.rs:3289-3400` verify different basenames only and explicitly codify basename slugging; there is no same-basename or normalization-collision case.
* `repo_slug_with`/DB `slug_for_repo` elsewhere can disambiguate repository paths, demonstrating that the config layer's identity is a separate lossy scheme.

## Impact

* A repository named like a trusted work repository can inherit its agent accounts, bundle credentials, writable sandbox mounts, hooks, network/merge policy, signing/Git settings, and automated supervisors.
* Merge/PR queues can run the wrong command, target the wrong branch, or auto-land under another repository's policy.
* Trusted hooks or CI/autopilot behavior intended for one repo can execute when operating on another.
* MCP scope ceilings and account selections can be widened or changed by accidental identity aliasing.
* Same-basename clones from different hosts/organizations are a normal workflow, so this does not require an exotic hash collision.
* Config explain/edit output cannot tell the user that one table ambiguously governs multiple authorities.

## Required remediation

1. Define one canonical, versioned repository identity from lossless platform path identity plus verified Git origin/repository identity, with an opaque collision-resistant ID and explicit aliases.
2. Key trusted workspace overlays by canonical ID. Human slugs may be labels or explicit aliases but must never silently select authority when ambiguous.
3. Resolve one immutable repository identity before applying any trusted overlay, hook, account/bundle, sandbox mount, queue, CI/autopilot, Git, or MCP policy.
4. Validate configuration globally: reject duplicate IDs, ambiguous aliases, empty/reserved keys, and alias normalization collisions. Provide an explicit, visible mapping command for user-friendly names.
5. Bind the resolved overlay and its config generation into downstream launch/queue attestations so a path/origin/config change cannot produce a hybrid policy.
6. Make CLI explain/edit/list surfaces show canonical repository identity, origin, alias, and every matching path. Refuse mutation or execution on ambiguous legacy keys.
7. Migrate legacy basename tables by enumerating known repositories. Preserve ambiguous entries and require user selection; never assign a high-authority block by current directory or first match.
8. Handle repository moves, origin changes, worktrees, mirrors, case-insensitive filesystems, non-UTF-8 paths, and multiple checkouts with an explicit identity policy.

## Acceptance criteria

* Tests cover two repositories with the same basename under different parents/origins, punctuation/case aliases, Unicode/non-UTF-8 paths, symlink/relative aliases, mirrors, worktrees, moves, and origin replacement.
* No colliding or ambiguous repository receives another's hooks, mounts, credentials, bundle/HOME, merge/PR targets or commands, CI/autopilot mode, Git policy, or MCP scopes.
* Configuration load/explain/edit fails visibly on ambiguous legacy aliases before any repo-influenced process or provider effect.
* The canonical overlay identity is stable where policy says it should be and generation-invalidated where path/origin authority changes.
* Queue and agent records retain the exact repository/config identity they were admitted under.
* Migration preserves every legacy block and requires an explicit mapping for same-basename repositories.
* User-friendly aliases remain possible but are uniqueness-checked and never authority-bearing by themselves.

## Dependency mapping

This blocks <issue id="f94f8554-b48e-47e8-a672-27e208e0dc48" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-233/credential-isolate-every-autonomous-issue-merge-pr-ci-and-review-agent">THE-233</issue> because agent credential and sandbox policy cannot be isolated when unrelated repositories share a trusted workspace overlay. It also blocks <issue id="76b4577a-8d92-4897-9494-e51c5d332297" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-397/gate-the-exact-candidate-tree-from-a-clean-declared-workspace">THE-397</issue>'s exact-candidate gate contract because merge gate selection can resolve through the wrong repository policy. Related to <issue id="3d3a566c-145a-4f99-a005-3a6e739f4753" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-268/bind-pipeline-claim-prompt-and-sandbox-launch-to-one-immutable-config">THE-268</issue> (immutable pipeline config revision), <issue id="0073f14d-55b8-44fe-924b-216235f376a4" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-366/make-workspace-clone-destinations-canonical-collision-resistant-and">THE-366</issue> (same-basename clone identity), <issue id="42561f86-f1b1-4223-9aff-b687865c366f" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-301/use-collision-resistant-lossless-path-identity-for-daemon-scope-and">THE-301</issue> (lossless path identity), <issue id="70d95fef-6065-4004-92bc-30a3b606c44d" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-444/make-named-profiles-canonical-fail-closed-credential-firewalls">THE-444</issue> (profile firewall), <issue id="490ed4c1-2764-4068-8456-91894d21731a" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-509/give-coding-agent-accounts-collision-proof-credential-home-identities">THE-509</issue>/<issue id="50b97895-d9c2-4dc4-9b8c-05103a2ce3fb" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-510/make-managed-bundle-homes-canonical-zone-safe-and-transactional">THE-510</issue> (account and bundle roots), and <issue id="eb394a24-e763-4f15-8257-2e3d9698cbda" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-513/bind-sandbox-container-names-and-reuse-to-canonical-instance">THE-513</issue> (sandbox instance identity).
